subject.title: fix: OpenAI OAuth works behind fake-IP proxies

question: Should the fake-IP exception cover the official OpenAI device-code token exchange as well as authorization-code and refresh exchanges, while custom or redirected hosts remain fail-closed?
rationale: The sibling device-code path shares the reported proxy-DNS failure mode but uses a separate request helper and configurable base-path context, so its permanent SSRF-policy boundary needs explicit owner confirmation.

options.title: Cover all official OAuth exchanges
options.body: Apply the exact-host `auth.openai.com` policy to device-code exchange too, preserve fail-closed handling for redirects and other hosts, and prove it through a real fake-IP proxy.

options.title: Keep device-code outside scope
options.body: Land only the authorization-code and refresh fix, but narrow the PR claim and document that device-code login remains unsupported behind fake-IP proxy DNS.

recommendation.title: Cover all official OAuth exchanges
recommendation.body: Apply the exact-host `auth.openai.com` policy to device-code exchange too, preserve fail-closed handling for redirects and other hosts, and prove it through a real fake-IP proxy.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest evidence-backed routing contact from recent merged OpenAI OAuth work that separated this SSRF-policy question for dedicated review.
